protocol.title: Node lesson 1 — Variables & wires
protocol.summary: A guided build: construct a two-input → equation workflow yourself, then watch the document read your numbers live. Opens in the ⬡ Nodes view with the tour running.

chips.text: you build it — nothing is pre-made

children.body: How this lesson works. It opens in the ⬡ Nodes view on an empty canvas, with a guided tour running: a pulsing ring points at the next control, the card in the top-right says what to do, and each step ticks off the moment you actually do it. This page is the reference; the canvas is the workbench. Reopen the lesson anytime — steps you've already done skip themselves.

A node is one box on the canvas, and each node makes one or more variables. You'll build two Input nodes — volume_each and replicates — that the person running the protocol sets with sliders, and one Equation node that computes total_volume from them. Units are picked, not typed: choose a Type (Volume, Mass, …) and the unit dropdown narrows to that dimension's real options (µL, mL, …).

Every variable has a dot on each side of its row. The right dot passes the variable out; the left dot plugs a value in. A wire carries one variable from a right dot to a left dot — the tour will have you drag both inputs into the equation.

Names are the contract. Equations use variables by name, and this document reads them by name too — that's why the tour asks for volume_each, replicates, and total_volume exactly. (Picking a unit type first auto-names a fresh node volume_01-style — just overwrite it with the lesson's exact name.) Rename carelessly and the wiring survives but the prose goes blind.

Formulas are built, never typed. On the Equation node, every wired variable becomes a button with a dimension alias — V1 for the first volume, X1 for unitless — and a pad of operators sits below. Tap a variable, an operator, a variable; anything that would break the math stays greyed out. Need a plain number? Use the small 123 slot — but a constant with a unit belongs in a wired Constant node. Tapped the wrong variable? Tap its chip in the strip and swap it for another.

Once wired, the numbers are live: each node's header shows its current value, and the equation recomputes the instant an input changes. Getting around is gesture-driven: new nodes land in open canvas (never on top of each other), the ⌖ in a node's header — or double-clicking its card — zooms straight to it, and double-clicking empty canvas Fits everything back in view. Made a wrong wire? Click it to delete it — or hold Shift and drag a line through several to cut them all. Nodes move by their header; wires reroute around the boxes on their own.

The writing reads the graph. Once you've built and named total_volume, you'll finish this very sentence with the Reference button in the ✎ Editor — click where the number belongs, pick the variable, and the live value drops in as a chip. No syntax to type, ever. Change a slider afterwards and the number follows. Before a value can be referenced it must be GATED: wire total_volume into a Cards node in the graph (the tour walks you through it) — that puts it on the document AND into the reference picker. Then finish the sentence: Total volume to prepare:

That's the whole idea: nodes make variables, wires move them, equations combine them, and the document reads the live values. When the tour finishes, open Lesson 2 to build bindings — wires that drive a node's settings.
